Artist Casey Curran creates kinetic sculptures that combine mechanical systems with forms inspired by plants and natural structures. In this prototype, layers of delicate petals are connected so that a single mechanical action produces a rippling movement across the entire structure. Instead of every element moving independently, the motion travels through the sculpture like a wave. This type of movement is central to Curran’s practice. Using motors, wires, cranks and carefully engineered mechanisms, he creates artificial flowers and organisms that bloom, flutter and contract.  The machinery is artificial, but the movement feels strangely organic ,engineering becomes a way of imitating the rhythms of living systems. #art #artist #fashion #avantgarde #design

Janel Hawkins, founder of Sand Castle University, transforms compacted sand into detailed sculptures, from elaborate castles to animals and imaginative characters. Carving away small sections and smoothing each surface, she gradually turns a simple mound into shapes with surprisingly crisp edges and intricate details. The process is mesmerizing to watch, especially knowing how temporary the finished work is. Each sculpture takes patience and precision, even though the sand will eventually lose its shape. “You Never Have to Smoke Alone” is a kinetic sculpture by Danish-Icelandic artist Jeppe Hein, known for creating interactive works that subtly reshape how viewers experience space. Using motion and air to form drifting, smoke-like shapes, the piece turns something fleeting into a shared visual moment. It emphasizes impermanence, presence, and quiet connection, inviting viewers to slow down and engage with the work as it unfolds in real time. #art #Sculpture ##artist##museum##museums

This is the clock that becomes digital from analog a stunning piece of kinetic art and engineering. Dozens of individual analog clocks are arranged in a grid on a large wall panel. Each clock has two independently controlled hands. When the time changes, every hand rotates in perfect coordination so that groups of clocks form the shapes of digital numbers. Six clocks typically work together to create one digit. Across the full wall they display hours and minutes in clear digital form, then smoothly transition to the next minute with a mesmerizing dance of moving hands. #clock #art  #worldrecord
